roundOneFindings: All five fixed at ee9ec60b: one live-tree definition (record/project.go line/liveRoots), RanAsRoot gates every RecordedAncestor write (workflow/adopt.go), re-read on a recorded issue's re-parent (repositories.go:761), settleObserved carries RecordedAncestor (intake/facts.go:799), one listing walk at boot and no walk for unlabelled issues; the per-event re-read is only partly bounded (finding 3).

keyFindings.description: recordedAncestor stops at the first recorded root on the chain (l.858), and returns '' when the parent itself is recorded (l.836), whether or not that root's tree is live. A labelled todo R under unrecorded P under Q, a recorded root parked in backlog under live T (a once-queued root a person moved under T, INFRA-214's state), is recorded with RecordedAncestor Q, not held (Q is not live), and takes a slot and an architect, though release_children's walk reaches T. Reproduced at ee9ec60b with a throwaway heldLine test: slotted=true, RecordedAncestor LEGION-180. Contradicts AGENTS.md:197-199 and the architect skill l.38.

l.39 tells an architect refused CHILD_IN_OTHER_TREE to re-parent the child back or ask that tree's architect. A todo child K of a root H held under the architect's tree is refused exactly so (`K runs in the tree of H, not T`, the tester's round-3 proof), and H has no architect; the remedy is to release H, which brings K. The guidance, or the refusal, must name that case.

Round-1 finding 5, partly open: every event of an unrecorded issue (any status) still re-walks the chain of every labelled todo root under an unrecorded parent (l.761, ParentedQueuedRoots includes roots under plain epics), one Dispatch read and one recordOf transaction per key, inside AckWait; a deadline expiry mid-walk is not an ancestorUnread and naks the unrelated event. prepareObserved (l.645) runs the same full re-read synchronously inside release_children's HTTP request for each unrecorded todo child, and settleObserved discards it once the child is recorded.

An out-of-order older event of a recorded issue whose parent differs from its record's (l.761) seeds the walk with its stale parent, and applyReread writes before admission's sequence fence, so a hold a newer re-parent removed comes back until the next re-read; T's release of that root answers 403 ISSUE_OUTSIDE_TREE meanwhile.
